edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Chronic psychological stress is plausibly linked to Cognitive function through mechanisms that fit its exposure class and target tissue, but the exact pathway depends on dose, timing, and baseline vulnerability. The best interpretation is usually that it changes the biologic setting in which Cognitive function develops rather than acting as a single on-off switch.
edges.summary: Chronic psychological stress appears tied to worse cognitive function in working-age adults mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
